chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no prayer on the day of Al-Fitr and Al-Adha except with an Imam.

key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفِطْرِ: The day of Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Eid prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that the Eid prayers are a communal obligation (fard kifayah) requiring the leadership of an Imam, distinguishing them from individual voluntary prayers. This ruling highlights the political and religious authority of the Imam in presiding over public worship, a concept central to both Twelver and Ismaili traditions regarding the visibility of divine guidance.
